findings.title: No re-check of the cache after taking the write lock
findings.body: Outside Dev mode, every request that reads a nil cache at line 42 (all concurrent requests at cold start, or every request after a load failure) waits on `Lock()` at line 48 and then rebuilds the manifest itself. Nothing checks whether the goroutine ahead of it already filled `entryPointAssetsCache`, so N concurrent callers open and decode `assets-manifest.json` N times, one after another. If the commented-out CDN path at line 54 is ever enabled, they would make N serial HTTP fetches while holding the lock. Add the standard double-check right after line 49: `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`.

contracts.action: GetWebAssets reads the global cache under RLock and rebuilds it under an exclusive Lock
contracts.equivalent_path: Before: an unsynchronized read and write of the package-level pointer. Callers: index.go, frontendsettings.go, recovery.go
contracts.before_after: Callers only read fields of the returned DTO (frontendsettings.go hashes ContentDeliveryURL/Dark/Light; recovery.go substitutes an empty DTO when it gets nil). Before it is cached, the DTO is mutated only once, by SetContentDeliveryURL under the write lock, so sharing the pointer after it is published is safe.
contracts.visible_effect: The index page and frontend settings get the same asset list as before. The data race in Dev mode, where every request rewrote the global, is gone. In Dev mode all index requests are now serialized on the write lock.
contracts.failure_mode: When the manifest read fails, the cache is set to nil and the error goes back to the caller (index.go returns it; recovery.go falls back to empty assets). The next request retries. Same behavior as before. There is no re-check after taking Lock, so concurrent cold-start callers each repeat the read.

summary: The PR's title says "Frontend Asset Optimization", but the change only adds an RWMutex around the global entry-point assets cache in GetWebAssets. That fixes the data race on the package-level pointer. Callers only read the returned DTO, so sharing it is safe. One optional improvement: after taking the write lock, the code doesn't check the cache again, so concurrent callers that find it empty each re-read the manifest in turn. No tests cover the concurrent path.
